name: Lesson 23 · Where and where to: in, auf, an… with the dative or the accusative

cards.front: The book is on **the table**.
cards.note: Two-way prepositions: wo? takes the dative. Where something is (wo?): auf + dative.

cards.front: The picture is hanging on **the wall**.
cards.note: Two-way prepositions: wo? takes the dative. an for a vertical surface; where it is, so dative: der Wand.

cards.front: The cat is sleeping under **the bed**.
cards.note: Two-way prepositions: wo? takes the dative. unter + dative for where: dem Bett.

cards.front: The bicycle is behind **the house**.
cards.note: Two-way prepositions: wo? takes the dative. hinter + dative: dem Haus.

cards.front: The pharmacy is next to **the bakery**.
cards.note: Two-way prepositions: wo? takes the dative. neben + dative: der Bäckerei.

cards.front: The lamp is hanging above **the table**.
cards.note: Two-way prepositions: wo? takes the dative. über + dative: above, where it is.

cards.front: The car is in front of **the house**.
cards.note: Two-way prepositions: wo? takes the dative. vor + dative: in front of.

cards.front: The cat is sitting between **the chairs**.
cards.note: Two-way prepositions: wo? takes the dative. zwischen + dative plural: den Stühlen, with -n.

cards.front: My mother is in **the kitchen**.
cards.note: Two-way prepositions: wo? takes the dative. in + dative for where: der Küche.

cards.front: Where is my key? – In **the bag**.
cards.back: Wo ist mein Schlüssel? – In **der Tasche**.
cards.note: Two-way prepositions: wo? takes the dative. wo? asks for a place, and the answer takes the dative.

cards.front: The children are playing **in the** garden.
cards.note: Two-way prepositions: wo? takes the dative. in dem becomes im: where, so dative.

cards.front: The milk is **in the** fridge.
cards.note: Two-way prepositions: wo? takes the dative. im = in dem. Bottles stand, so steht.

cards.front: I'm **at the** station.
cards.note: Two-way prepositions: wo? takes the dative. an dem becomes am: at the station.

cards.front: We live **in** Berlin.
cards.note: Two-way prepositions: wo? takes the dative. in + a town, no article.

cards.front: I'm putting the book on **the table**.
cards.back: Ich lege das Buch auf **den Tisch**.
cards.note: Two-way prepositions: wohin? takes the accusative. Where to (wohin?): auf + accusative, den Tisch.

cards.front: I'm putting the milk in **the fridge**.
cards.back: Ich stelle die Milch in **den Kühlschrank**.
cards.note: Two-way prepositions: wohin? takes the accusative. A movement to a place: accusative, den Kühlschrank.

cards.front: He's hanging the picture on **the wall**.
cards.back: Er hängt das Bild an **die Wand**.
cards.note: Two-way prepositions: wohin? takes the accusative. an + accusative for where to: die Wand.

cards.front: The cat runs under **the bed**.
cards.note: Two-way prepositions: wohin? takes the accusative. It moves there, so accusative: das Bett.

cards.front: She's going into **the kitchen**.
cards.note: Two-way prepositions: wohin? takes the accusative. Going in: in + accusative, die Küche.

cards.front: Put the bike behind **the house**! (one friend)
cards.note: Two-way prepositions: wohin? takes the accusative. A change of place: hinter + accusative.

cards.front: I'm putting the chair between **the table** and the window.
cards.back: Ich stelle den Stuhl zwischen **den Tisch** und das Fenster.
cards.note: Two-way prepositions: wohin? takes the accusative. zwischen + accusative for where to: den Tisch.

cards.front: Where are you going? (one friend) – Into **town**.
cards.note: Two-way prepositions: wohin? takes the accusative. wohin? asks for a direction; the answer takes the accusative.

cards.front: We're going **to the** cinema.
cards.note: Two-way prepositions: wohin? takes the accusative. in das becomes ins: into, so accusative.

cards.front: **Put** the books on the shelf! (several friends)
cards.note: Two-way prepositions: wohin? takes the accusative. ins Regal: into the shelf, accusative. stellen for books upright.

cards.front: The glass **is** on the table.
cards.note: stehen/stellen, liegen/legen, hängen: being somewhere, putting it there. Upright things stehen; stehen is where something is, so the dative follows.

cards.front: I **put** the glass on the table.
cards.back: Ich **stelle** das Glas auf den Tisch.
cards.note: stehen/stellen, liegen/legen, hängen: being somewhere, putting it there. stellen: to put something upright; it moves, so the accusative follows.

cards.front: The newspaper **is lying** on the bed.
cards.note: stehen/stellen, liegen/legen, hängen: being somewhere, putting it there. Flat things liegen: dative, where it is.

cards.front: **Put** the newspaper on the bed! (one friend)
cards.note: stehen/stellen, liegen/legen, hängen: being somewhere, putting it there. legen: to lay something flat; accusative, where to.

cards.front: The coat **is hanging** in the wardrobe.
cards.note: stehen/stellen, liegen/legen, hängen: being somewhere, putting it there. hängen for where it hangs: im Schrank, dative.

cards.front: I **hang** my coat in the wardrobe.
cards.back: Ich **hänge** meinen Mantel in den Schrank.
cards.note: stehen/stellen, liegen/legen, hängen: being somewhere, putting it there. hängen for putting it there: in den Schrank, accusative. The same verb does both.

cards.front: The books **are** on the shelf.
cards.note: stehen/stellen, liegen/legen, hängen: being somewhere, putting it there. Books upright on a shelf stehen.

cards.front: The child **is sitting** at the table.
cards.note: stehen/stellen, liegen/legen, hängen: being somewhere, putting it there. sitzen: where someone sits, so the dative: am Tisch.

cards.front: Where **did** you **put** my key? (one friend)
cards.note: stehen/stellen, liegen/legen, hängen: being somewhere, putting it there. Wohin? asks where to: legen, regular, gelegt.

cards.front: Where are the glasses? – They **are** in the cupboard.
cards.back: Wo sind die Gläser? – Sie **stehen** im Schrank.
cards.note: stehen/stellen, liegen/legen, hängen: being somewhere, putting it there. German says where things stand or lie where English just says are.

cards.front: The keys **are** under the newspaper.
cards.note: stehen/stellen, liegen/legen, hängen: being somewhere, putting it there. Keys lie flat: liegen, and unter + dative.
